items.title: Use provenance-backed collisional coefficients and pressure shifts
items.problem: The current low-order constants can imply false precision: an Rb self-broadening coefficient can reach Cs, Ne is represented by a fixed broadening-only scalar, pressure shift is absent, and added homogeneous widths do not enter all OD/SAS pump and probe paths consistently.
evidence: The 2026-07-20, 2026-07-30, and 2026-08-05 OD/SAS reviews independently identified coefficient fallback and pump/probe linewidth mismatches.
The 2026-07-23, 2026-07-28, and 2026-08-03 Magneto reviews found that the collisional data API cannot distinguish the optical effects later needed by the Liouvillian.
The 2026-08-06 Lambda review confirmed that pressure shift/broadening provenance remains unresolved.

ElecSus derives self-broadening in closed form per line, gamma_self = 2*pi*gamma_0*N*(lambda/(2*pi))^3 with an additional factor sqrt(2) on D2 (libs/spectra.py). That form reproduces the Rb-85 D1 coefficient hard-coded here (7.3e-8 against the 6.9e-8 Hz cm^3 value used, about 6% high) while scaling on its own to Rb D2 (1.0e-7), Cs D1 (8.3e-8), and Cs D2 (1.2e-7), whereas species.self_broadened_gamma ignores its isotope argument and applies the single Rb value to every species and line.
acceptance_criteria: Each collisional coefficient type used by the listed OD/SAS, Magneto, and Lambda paths has the physically required gas/species/line keys and validity domain, plus source, units, sign, and uncertainty.
Unsupported combinations return an explicit unsupported/qualitative status instead of falling back to another species or line.
Pressure-shift coefficients carry an explicit frequency convention and are applied once to the detuning with tested sign and unit conversions.
The coefficient API returns pressure shift and elastic optical dephasing separately; magneto-dynamics-semantics exclusively owns their Liouvillian application.
OD/SAS pump and probe paths use one documented homogeneous-width convention.

At zero buffer-gas pressure, buffer-gas shift and dephasing are exactly zero while species/line-specific self-broadening remains density dependent; unaffected Rb-85 D1 anchors remain unchanged and corrected fallback cases are checked against their own sourced references.
out_of_scope: Phenomenological Dicke-narrowing knobs without a validation dataset.
FWM coefficient or Rabi-model changes in pass 1; existing FWM baselines must remain unchanged.

items.problem: Resolved: core and the compiled kernel now support arbitrary finite N_F>=1 by block continued fractions, while an independently assembled dense extended block pins N_F=1,2,3. The frozen baseline was intentionally versioned with its previous N_F=1 anchors preserved.
acceptance_criteria: A slow generalized reference supports at least N_F=1, 2, and 3; direct block and continued-fraction solutions agree below 1e-10 where both are well conditioned.
For every order, Tr rho_0=1, nonzero-harmonic traces vanish, and normalized linear-system residuals are below 1e-10.

Every reported scan uses N_F>=3. Dimensionless transfer coefficients satisfy |Delta T| <= 1e-10+0.01 max(|T_N|,|T_N-1|); each reduced-susceptibility component uses the unit-aware full-scan rule |Delta chi| <= 0.01 max(|chi_N|,|chi_N-1|)+1e-8 max_scan(|chi|), so a fixed SI absolute tolerance cannot hide an order-unity response change. Wrapped transfer phases differ by less than 0.5 degree only where both amplitudes exceed 1e-8 max(1,||T||_infinity); below that floor the mixed complex-coefficient criterion applies and no phase is reported.

The optimum-detuning shift is no greater than one final-grid interval for each explicitly allowed mean-field objective such as a G_p peak. An optimum of the historical gain-only diagnostic is labelled historical and cannot be called a physical squeezing optimum.
A single operating-point N_F=2/3 agreement cannot certify a scan; any failed criterion returns UNCONVERGED instead of a best-looking value.
The compiled kernel matches the generalized reference at each supported order before becoming the production default.
Liouvillian half-plane, positivity, trace, and Hermiticity remain assembly invariants and cannot substitute for Floquet truncation convergence.

items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/layout/ holds two coordinate systems that never mix: `display` (Node.x/y/angle, Link.via) draws the table, `path_m` does the physics, and neither is derived from the other. Results are unchanged, and the bridge in fact now reproduces a hand-driven GABES run to exactly zero at both Fast and Ultra. items.title: Bidirectional Streamlit canvas component: click -> Python
items.why: GROUP B. DONE, and the fallback is not needed. A hand-written bidirectional component works: sabes/components/canvas.py declares the component over a static frontend/index.html that implements the postMessage protocol (streamlit:componentReady / setFrameHeight / setComponentValue) in vanilla JS, with no npm, no lockfile and no build step -- it ships as package data. Verified against the running app at ?app=sabes&dev=canvas: the component loads and sizes its own frame; clicking an optic returns its id; clicking empty table returns a coordinate in SPEC units, checked at three different render scales including 0.42x, where a naive screen-pixel reading would have been wrong by more than a factor of two; and a repeat click on the same optic still re-fires, because Streamlit reruns only when a component value CHANGES and every event therefore carries a monotonic seq. One real bug was caught and fixed on the way: exporting the drawing function as `canvas` from the package __init__ shadowed the submodule of the same name, so it is now `svg_canvas`. CONFIRMED on Streamlit Community Cloud, which was the actual point of the spike: all four checks pass on the deployed app at ?app=sabes&dev=canvas, with the coordinate round-trip exact at the 1.06x render scale the deployment happens to use. Deployment also surfaced one thing local testing could not: Community Cloud wraps the app in a second same-origin iframe, so the browser-tab retitling reached only the wrapper and the real tab kept its old name -- the title observer now targets window.top rather than window.parent. Delete sabes/components/spike.py and its ?dev=canvas route once the table view lands.

items.title: Optical-table view reproducing the two setup drawings
items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/layout/render.py turns a layout plus the live source chain into a canvas spec; sabes_page.py shows it as the first tab, one part at a time. Optics are drawn as glyphs built from sub-primitives inside a single clickable group (a polarizing cube is a square plus its diagonal, an etalon a plate plus its two faces), so a rich shape does not fragment into separate click targets. Glyph choice is matched on the id's own vocabulary rather than a per-node styling field, so adding an optic needs no renderer change and an unmatched node still draws. Two conventions are enforced by test: stroke width encodes POWER logarithmically and is not beam size (a 530 um beam on a metre of table is 0.05 percent of the width -- drawn honestly it would be invisible), and the legend says so; and shape clickability is exactly Node.clickable, so 'clickable' and 'modelled' cannot drift apart. Colours reuse the setup drawings' own key. Clicking an optic selects it and shows what it owns; clicking anywhere else drops a probe and reports the beam there via beam_at, with power, radius and the segment's provenance. Editing in place is Stage D. Three implementation findings worth keeping: (1) a component's value only reaches Python at the START of a run, so panels rendered after the canvas read the previous selection -- the handler now signals a rerun rather than letting the readout trail one click behind; (2) Streamlit does not re-lay-out a custom component that first mounts inside an inactive tab, so the second canvas stayed pinned at 300x0 -- the part selector is a radio, not nested tabs, which also halves the work per rerun; (3) the frontend now re-reports its height from a ResizeObserver instead of only on window resize. items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/instruments/ holds power meter, beam profiler, wavemeter, photodiode, oscilloscope and spectrum analyser. items.title: Return the dispersive partner of the OD/SAS absorption profile
items.problem: The OD/SAS spectrum is assembled from unit-area absorption Lorentzians only, so the real part of the susceptibility is never formed. Refractive index, accumulated phase, polarization rotation, and group index are unavailable on the one scheme that owns the validated hyperfine absolute scale, and any later polarimetric or Faraday/Voigt readout would have no dispersive input to propagate.
evidence: schemes/sas.py builds each hyperfine component as a unit-area Lorentzian (hwhm/pi)/(arg^2 + hwhm^2) and sums absorption only; observables.py exposes transmission and optical_density from alpha, while observables.group_index has no OD/SAS caller.

ElecSus obtains absorption and dispersion from a single Faddeeva evaluation of one complex line profile and reuses the real part for refractive index, rotation angle, and group index (libs/spectra.py, add_voigt).
items.why: DONE. Each hyperfine component now contributes one complex profile, chi_t = (A_t/k)*i/(pi*(Gamma_eff/2 - i*delta_t)): the imaginary part is the unit-area lineshape that already built alpha and the real part is its Kramers-Kronig partner, both weighted by the same velocity-resolved population difference and the same Doppler quadrature, so a pumped spectrum reports the saturated medium's dispersion. The generic path takes both quadratures from the one weak-probe susceptibility it already solved. compute() returns chi_real_unit and k_vec; observables scales it with the same line-strength factor as alpha and adds a Dispersion view (n - 1 in ppm, ASCII axis labels) plus a Peak phase shift metric. observables.refractive_index and observables.single_pass_phase now hold the dilute-vapor convention that group_index also calls. alpha is bit-for-bit unchanged on seven species/line/pump/coating cases checked against the previous revision, so the AutoOD anchor is untouched. Both quadratures agree with an independent scipy Faddeeva Voigt reference to 3e-4 at 25 C and 90 C, and the homogeneous-limit sign is pinned by a two-level OBE fixture (Re chi / Im chi = -delta/hwhm to 2e-8, n > 1 below resonance). No group-index readout is exposed.
acceptance_criteria: Absorption and dispersion for each hyperfine component come from one complex lineshape evaluation with a documented sign and frequency convention, not from two independently normalized profiles.

The dispersive component carries the same velocity-resolved population difference and the same Doppler quadrature as the absorption; a weak-probe dispersion is never paired with a saturated absorption spectrum.
A Kramers-Kronig or analytic-Voigt fixture checks the returned real part against an independent reference in both the homogeneous limit and a Doppler-broadened case.
The pump-off Rb-85 D1 AutoOD absolute anchor remains within its documented 0.1% tolerance.
Any refractive-index or group-index readout reuses observables.group_index instead of a scheme-local re-implementation, and states whether it is a phase or a group quantity.

items.title: One CSV text decoder and one read-only array converter
items.problem: experimental_csv._decode_csv and rydberg_experimental_csv._decode were the same encoding cascade (BOM UTF-16, UTF-8, CP949, Latin-1) apart from the exception type, and _readonly was written three times (experimental_csv, rydberg_experimental_csv, vapor_cell, which rydberg_experiment imports), one of them freezing in place instead of copying.
items.why: Consolidation item 10 of the 2026-10-30 survey under the unified-engine principle (AGENTS.md).
acceptance_criteria: Every loader returns bit-identical traces, diagnostics, provenance and error messages for every encoding branch, and every converter keeps its copy/alias behaviour.

validation_scope.method: Frozen copy of gabes/ before and after (only _arrays.py, _csv_numeric.py, experimental_csv.py, rydberg_experimental_csv.py and vapor_cell.py differ); recursive leaf comparison with return types, array dtypes, read-only flags and, for the converters, whether the result aliases its input and whether the input stays writeable.
validation_scope.cases: Both decoders over UTF-16 LE/BE BOM, malformed UTF-16, UTF-8 with and without BOM, CP949 and two Latin-1 fallbacks, plus short and empty input; load_experimental_csv on those payloads with and without denoising, both absolute calibrations, a forward/reverse sweep and a non-bytes input; transform_x; load_eit_csv, load_rf_sweep_csv and load_psd_csv in five encodings plus CP949, whitespace, malformed and empty sources; the four read-only converters on float, int, list, view, read-only, scalar and float32 inputs; and the item-8 vapor-cell/rydberg_experiment snapshot (379 entries) rerun on both trees.

items.review_note: ⟦AI⟧ _csv_numeric.decode_csv_text(data, error) takes the loader's exception class for malformed UTF-16; both loaders call it. _arrays.readonly_float_array(values, copy=True) replaces the three converters; experimental_csv binds copy=False because its version froze the freshly computed arrays in place (np.asarray), the others copied. Recorded, not changed: the cascade's plain 'utf-8' step is unreachable (utf-8-sig accepts the same bytes), so BOM-less UTF-8 is labelled 'utf-8-sig' in provenance; the two byte readers (_coerce_bytes and _read_source) differ in accepted sources, limits and UI-visible messages and stay separate. The landing replaces the stale staged deletion of gabes/_csv_numeric.py in the shared index (working copy was identical to HEAD) with the new blob. tests/test_csv_shared.py covers every decoding branch, each loader's error type, the copy flag and the routed callers.

Phase 2b-1 moved g_J/g_I into species.Isotope with species.lande_gf for magneto_multilevel and schemes/magneto.py, bit-identically. Still separate: the Zeeman generator per magneto path, because magneto_multilevel forms (µ_B/ħ)·g_F and schemes/magneto.py (µ_B·g_F)/ħ, which differ in the last bit for Rb87 F=2. Also separate: gabes/fwm_zeeman_response.py (another session, uncommitted) assembles its own 24-level AtomModel and reset from build_multilevel_atom; fwm.thermal_transit_reset_superoperator; quantum.reservoirs ExplicitReservoirs.dissipator and thermal_reset_channels, whose real-identity kron can differ from core.dissipator in signed zeros. The magneto speed patch these steps waited on landed in 695311b.
acceptance_criteria: One Zeeman-Hamiltonian helper serves both magneto paths only after the user accepts the last-bit change; otherwise Rb85/Rb87 magneto outputs stay bit-identical.
build_multilevel_atom keeps its outputs, level order, signed dipoles, normalization and read-only cached arrays for FWM.
Every step is a snapshot-verified bit-identical refactor; value changes are separate decisions, and moved source-hash receipts are reported, not resealed.
quantum.reservoirs either keeps byte parity with its sealed records or stays a documented independent assembly.
fwm.thermal_transit_reset_superoperator joins only once `git status` shows gabes/schemes/fwm.py clean; another session's edits there are in flight.
Retiring zeeman.rb85_d1_double_lambda_zeeman, or deriving any builder from species.level_structure, is a separate value decision; the retirement also waits for a clean gabes/schemes/fwm.py.
A shared resolved-Zeeman AtomModel view is extracted from gabes/fwm_zeeman_response.py's own arithmetic only after that file is committed, so its outputs stay bit-identical.

items.title: ⟦AI⟧ 컴파일 LU 실패 상태·계산점 진단 계약 보완

items.title: ⟦AI⟧ GABES·SABES 공용 렌더링 동기화 범위 점검
items.problem: ⟦AI⟧ GABES는 plotcard.PLOT_LOCK을 사용하고 SABES는 별도 _PLOT_LOCK을 사용한다. SABES _cached_observables와 Spectrum 그림 표시 경로에는 동일한 보호 범위가 명시되어 있지 않다. 공유 Matplotlib 상태에 대한 정적 보호 범위 점검 과제이며, 실제 race/crash나 락 경합 병목을 재현했다는 뜻은 아니다.
acceptance_criteria: ⟦AI⟧ 두 화면의 figure 생성·mathtext/layout·artist 변경·복사·draw/export·표시·정리 경로와 lock 소유권을 목록화하고, 같은 프로세스의 공유 Matplotlib 상태가 일관된 동기화 범위에 있는지 확인한다.
⟦AI⟧ 병렬 호출·캐시 cold/warm·중첩 렌더링·예외 복원 fixture로 오류와 세션 간 figure/label 혼입, 교착 및 lock 해제를 검증한다. 보호가 필요한 경로는 동등한 동기화를 유지한다.
⟦AI⟧ Figure() 직접 생성이나 Agg 사용만으로 thread safety를 선언하지 않는다. 기존 보호를 제거하거나 락 범위를 줄이려면 대체 보호와 동시 실행 검증 근거를 먼저 제시한다.
⟦AI⟧ 원자 계산과 lock 대기·그림 생성/렌더 시간을 분리해 경합을 측정하고, 수치 결과·headless API·표시 및 export 계약을 보존한다. 측정 없이 병목이나 속도 개선을 확정하지 않는다.
evidence: ⟦AI⟧ streamlit_app._cached_observables는 PLOT_LOCK으로 보호된다. SABES의 별도 lock은 일부 trace 그림에 사용되지만 _cached_observables/Spectrum에는 같은 범위가 드러나지 않는다. 완료된 headless 분리와 별개의 점검이다.
